summary: CI deploy runner: service-account scope mismatch after scheduled secrets rotation causing intermittent release failures
description:
Issue summary:
Scheduled key rotation for the CI service-account (svc-ci-deployer) completed last night but several deploy jobs in the morning release pipeline started failing with permission errors. Failures are intermittent across runner pools and are blocking the 2026-03-10 09:00 release window.

Impact:
- Release pipelines failing (canary and prod-promote) intermittently, ~30% of deploy jobs failed across the last 2 hours.
- Engineers on-call unable to promote critical bugfix.
- Potential regression risk if we roll back rotation without fixing scope mapping.

Environment:
- Production CI clusters, us-east region.
- Runners: ephemeral fleet (auto-provisioned) and a small set of persistent deploy runners.
- Secrets backend: Vault (managed), rotation job triggered by infra-scheduler.

Steps to reproduce:
1) Trigger a deploy pipeline that uses svc-ci-deployer to create/patch k8s deployments and upload artifacts to s3.
2) Observe auth failures when runner tries to perform iam:passRole / s3:PutObject on target resources.
3) Rerunning the job sometimes succeeds (racey/auth cache behavior).

Observed behavior:
- Error seen in pipeline logs: "403 AccessDenied: iam:PassRole is not allowed for principal arn:aws:sts::123456789012:assumed-role/svc-ci-deployer/runner-xxxx"
- Vault rotation job logs show new key created and old key revoked at 02:13 UTC.
- Some runners still hold old credentials; some pick up new credentials but with a narrower role policy (missing passRole on deploy-role).

Expected behavior:
- Rotation should swap credentials without changing assigned IAM role/policy scope; runners should smoothly pick up new credentials via the vault-agent sync.

Temporary workaround:
- Manually reassign the deploy role to svc-ci-deployer in IAM for failing jobs (performed by infra-oncall).
- Rolling deploy of persistent runners with forced vault-agent restart mitigates the failures for those runners.

Notes:
- This looks like a post-rotation policy mismatch between the new credentials and the expected deploy role or a vault sync hook that rewrites the attached policy to a default narrower template.
- Affected release: 2026-03-10 canary/prod promotion.
investigation_notes:
(2026-03-10 09:35) Checked Vault rotation job: rotation succeeded and new credential metadata: key_id=rot-20260310-09, issuance=2026-03-10T02:13:10Z.
(2026-03-10 09:50) Pulled runner logs from runner-manager in us-east: several runners show Vault token refresh but subsequent STS assume-role returns an IAM policy that lacks iam:PassRole.
(2026-03-10 10:05) Hypothesis A: Rotation pipeline uses a template that omitted passRole for deploy-role in last deploy of infra-roles.
(2026-03-10 10:22) Hypothesis B: Vault sync job applied a default scoped policy for ephemeral identities; persistent svc account expected broader policy but was overwritten by sync.
(2026-03-10 10:45) Commands run:
- curl -s "https://vault.internal/api/creds/svc-ci-deployer/metadata/rot-20260310-09" | jq '.'
- aws iam get-role-policy --role-name deploy-role --policy-name svc-ci-deployer-access
- kubectl logs runner-abc -n ci | grep "AccessDenied"

Observations:
- The role-policy attached in IAM for deploy-role shows passRole allowed in the inline policy, but the temp credentials' policy (from STS) returned by the assume-role call lacks that action.
- Slack thread: #infra-runner (link: https://slack.redwood.com/archives/C01234ABC) contains initial alerts and manual fixes.

2026-03-10 09:42 - Maya Chen: Confirmed rotation completed at 02:13 UTC. Repro steps outlined above. Assigning to Arjun for deeper auth investigation.
2026-03-10 10:10 - Arjun Patel: Investigating – pulled vault and runner-manager logs. Suspect template drift in rotation job. Will validate template history and PRs.

2026-03-10 11:05 - Priya Rao (SRE): Applied provisional workaround: restarted vault-agent on 6 persistent deploy runners; those runners succeeded subsequently. Still seeing failures on ephemeral pool.
resolution: In progress - root cause not yet confirmed. Current mitigation: restart vault-agent on affected persistent runners and manually reassign deploy-role where needed. Next steps: (1) audit rotation job templates/commits between 2026-03-09 and 2026-03-10, (2) add end-to-end test for post-rotation assumed-role policy check, (3) implement a canary rotation workflow that verifies IAM policy actions (including iam:PassRole and s3:PutObject) before revoking old keys.
next_steps:
1) Arjun to review infra-scheduler rotation PRs and template revisions (target 2026-03-12).
2) SRE to add an automated post-rotation IAM smoke test into rotation pipeline (PR: infra-tools).
3) Release engineering to delay further release promotions until rotation validation is in place.
4) Plan a rollback path for rotation if tests fail in next run.
workaround_status: Partial - manual restarts and IAM adjustments temporarily reduce failures but do not fully prevent ephemeral runner failures.
notes_for_hand_off: If reassigning to another engineer, include access to: Vault rotation job logs, IAM console, runner-manager Grafana dashboard, and infra-scheduler pipeline history. Link to slack thread: https://slack.redwood.com/archives/C01234ABC
